description: Minimal scientifically valid multi-chain lattice-polymer aggregation model. Extends the validated single-chain ISAW replica-exchange architecture (remd_uniform_chain_2_new.py) to M identical self-avoiding chains in a periodic cubic box, reusing the single-chain fitted contact free energy without refitting. This document is the model/software CONTRACT; it deliberately does NOT hard-code one set of runtime parameters (M, N, L, temperatures, lambda values). Those are chosen per run and recorded in each run's output metadata.

spec_revision_history.change: Initial contract. The reduced potential was fixed to a single linear form u = b(T)*[lambda_intra*m_intra + lambda_inter*m_inter].
The authoritative reduced potential delegates the intrachain term to the selected model's single-chain potential while keeping interchain contacts linear.

hs and saturating_cooperative_contact now apply their complete single-chain Hamiltonian to m_total = m_intra + m_inter, normalized by total beads M*N when required. Unequal intra/inter lambda values are rejected for these models. Contact-quadratic models retain the revision-2 split rule.

Corrects revision 3, which incorrectly required lambda_intra == lambda_inter for hs. hs is LINEAR in the contact count, so u = b(T)*[lambda_intra*m_intra + lambda_inter*m_inter] is an exact Hamiltonian for INDEPENDENT lambdas and reduces to the label-blind form when they are equal; forcing equality removed the (1,0) collapse-only and (0,1) association-only controls without any physical justification. Only saturating_cooperative_contact is nonlinear in m and still requires one common contact scale. Also documents the saturating model's cooperativity rule ('global', default, unchanged; or 'local', per-monomer contact degree).

Adds local_coordination_saturation as a distinct fitted model. Its complete state is the nonbonded degree histogram h_0 through h_6 and its Hamiltonian is b(T)*m_total - A0*sum_i g(k_i), with q_i=k_i/2. It always uses local cooperativity, counts intra- and interchain neighbours identically, and requires one common contact scale. The historical saturating_cooperative_contact global default and every pre-existing Hamiltonian are unchanged.

system.number_of_chains_meaning: number of identical, connected self-avoiding chains simulated simultaneously
system.beads_per_chain_meaning: beads per chain (chain length); n_steps = N - 1 covalent bonds per chain
system.box_size_meaning: side length of the periodic cubic lattice box (integer); wrapped lattice sites number L^3
system.excluded_volume: Each wrapped lattice site may contain at most one bead (single occupancy).
system.minimum_box_size_reason: L < 3 creates ambiguous nearest-neighbor wrapping (a bead's +d and -d neighbor sites can coincide); such boxes are rejected.

volume_fraction.meaning: monomer volume fraction: fraction of the L^3 lattice sites occupied by beads. Must satisfy phi <= 1 (M*N <= L^3).

unwrapped.role: AUTHORITATIVE representation for chain connectivity and per-chain geometry (radius of gyration).
unwrapped.notes: Unwrapped coordinates are contiguous along each chain: consecutive bonded beads differ by exactly one lattice step (unit Manhattan distance). A chain may extend beyond [0, L); it is never wrapped for geometry.
unwrapped.canonicalization: After an ACCEPTED move, the moved chain is re-based by an integer multiple of L per axis so its bead 0 lies in the primary box [0, L)^3. This bounds unwrapped magnitudes (preventing whole-chain-translation drift to infinity) while preserving wrapped coordinates, occupancy, site_owner, connectivity, all contact counts, per-chain Rg, and the reduced potential. Canonicalization never runs on trial coordinates before the contact-delta evaluation.

wrapped.role: Derived (coord mod L). Used for occupancy, excluded-volume checks, contact counting, and interchain collision tests.
wrapped.definition: wrapped = ((unwrapped % L) + L) % L, applied component-wise so results lie in [0, L).
wrapped.notes: A chain crossing a periodic boundary must retain the correct Rg after using the unwrapped coordinates; wrapped coordinates are used only for occupancy and contacts.

occupancy.representation: mapping from wrapped lattice site (x, y, z) in [0, L)^3 to a unique global bead ID (NOT merely a set).
occupancy.global_id_inverse: chain_index = global_id // N ; monomer_index = global_id % N

contacts.authoritative_statement: Raw lattice contact counts m_intra and m_inter are AUTHORITATIVE. Every contact is counted exactly once, canonicalized as the unordered global-ID pair (min_id, max_id).

m_intra.definition: number of unique nonbonded nearest-neighbor contacts between beads on the SAME chain (wrapped nearest neighbors), counted once per unordered pair.
m_intra.bonded_exclusion: Covalently bonded nearest neighbors (same chain, |monomer_i - monomer_j| == 1) MUST NOT be counted as intrachain contacts.

m_inter.definition: number of unique nearest-neighbor contacts between beads on DIFFERENT chains (wrapped nearest neighbors), counted once per unordered pair.
m_inter.bonded_exclusion: Not applicable (different chains share no covalent bond); all interchain nearest-neighbor pairs count.

contacts.counting_rule: For every occupied bead, examine its six wrapped nearest-neighbor sites, retrieve any neighboring bead owner, canonicalize the pair as (min_id, max_id) so it is counted exactly once, classify as intra (same chain) or inter (different chains), and exclude covalently bonded same-chain neighbors. Integer counts throughout.

contact_offset.statement: Any molecular-to-lattice contact offset stored in the single-chain fit is excluded from the raw multi-chain contact counts and Hamiltonian.
contact_offset.reason: The offset was fitted for single-chain intrachain contact-number support alignment during free-energy fitting; it must not be applied to interchain contacts or to raw lattice counts used for sampling.

contact_normalization.purpose: Raw m_intra and m_inter are extensive, globally-unique contact-PAIR counts and remain the Hamiltonian variables. Intensive per-chain normalizations (dividing by the number of chains M) are added for ANALYSIS ONLY so runs with different M can be compared. They do not modify sampling, energy, or acceptance.

interpretation.m_inter_pairs_per_chain: globally-unique interchain contact PAIRS divided by M (each interchain contact counted once globally).
interpretation.m_inter_incidences_per_chain: average number of interchain-contact ENDPOINTS (incidences) associated with a chain; each interchain pair contributes one incidence to each of its two participating chains, hence the factor of 2.
interpretation.naming_rule: The two interchain normalizations are named distinctly (pairs vs incidences); neither is called simply 'm_inter_per_chain' because that would be scientifically ambiguous.

contact_normalization.scope: Comparisons across M should use the normalized quantities IN ADDITION to the raw totals. Normalization removes the leading extensive dependence on chain number only; it does NOT remove all finite-size or concentration effects.
contact_normalization.invariance: Normalized contacts, like raw contacts, are never rescaled by rg_scale (they are counts, not lengths).

reduced_potential.equation: Linear models (hs): u(X,T) = b(T)*[lambda_intra*m_intra + lambda_inter*m_inter] + kappa_bend*n_bend_total, with INDEPENDENT lambdas. saturating_cooperative_contact: u(X,T) = lambda_contact*u_contact(m_total,T;M*N) + kappa_bend*n_bend_total, with lambda_contact = lambda_intra = lambda_inter. local_coordination_saturation: u(X,T) = lambda_contact*[b(T)*m_total - A0*sum_i g(k_i)] + kappa_bend*n_bend_total, with q_i=k_i/2 and equal lambdas. Contact-quadratic models: lambda_intra*sum_alpha u_contact(m_intra_alpha,T;N) + lambda_inter*b(T)*m_inter + kappa_bend*n_bend_total.
reduced_potential.sampling_weight: P(X | T) proportional to exp(-u(X, T))
reduced_potential.structure: Contact term plus a separate additive bending term. The contact term takes one of four forms according to potential_kind: a linear intra/inter split with independent lambdas, a label-blind term in m_total for the historical saturating model, a sum over local monomer coordination for local_coordination_saturation, or the retained per-chain intrachain plus linear interchain rule for the contact-quadratic family. No term is folded into another.

linear_split_contact_term.delegation: b(T) is the selected model's own reduced_bias, taken unchanged from the single-chain fit. The multi-chain layer never refits it.
linear_split_contact_term.independent_lambdas: lambda_intra and lambda_inter are INDEPENDENT. Exactness follows from linearity of u_contact in m; see label_blindness_criterion.
linear_split_contact_term.move_delta_rule: b(T) * [lambda_intra * d_intra + lambda_inter * d_inter], exact for any move because the potential is linear in both counts.
linear_split_contact_term.normalization: None. The linear model needs no chain length; N is recorded as provenance only.
linear_split_contact_term.reduction: At lambda_intra == lambda_inter == lambda this is identically lambda * b(T) * m_total, i.e. the label-blind equal-contact null model.

label_blind_contact_term.delegation: u_contact is the selected model's complete single-chain contact potential, taken unchanged from reduced_contact_potential.

supported_potential_kinds.saturating_cooperative: u_contact(m,T;N) = N*[b(T)*q - A0*q^2/(1 + (q/q_sat)^2)] with q = m/N

label_blind_contact_term.why_label_blind: u_contact is NONLINEAR in m, so the intra/inter split cannot be carried through it and unequal lambda values are rejected.
label_blind_contact_term.identity_invariance: Under cooperativity='global', only m_total enters: repartitioning a fixed number of contacts between intra- and interchain classes or among chains cannot change the energy.
label_blind_contact_term.normalization: For cooperativity='global', q = m_total/(M*N), preserving an intensive contact density and an extensive total potential.

cooperativity_rule.global: Unchanged. The fitted single-chain Hamiltonian is applied once to m_total with M*N beads. At small q the cooperative term is -A0*m_total^2/(M*N), an all-to-all coupling between every pair of contacts in the box: non-additive over non-interacting chains and blind to WHERE the contacts are.
cooperativity_rule.local: u = lambda_contact * [b(T)*m_total - A0*sum_i g(k_i)] with g(k) = kappa^2/(1 + (kappa/q_sat)^2), kappa = k/2, and k_i the nonbonded contact degree of monomer i counting BOTH intra- and interchain neighbours. Since sum_i k_i = 2*m_total, kappa is the local analogue of q = m/N; at uniform degree k_i = 2m/N the sum reproduces the fitted single-chain cooperative term EXACTLY with the same A0 and q_sat, so no refit is involved. Being a sum of strictly local terms it is exactly additive over separated chains.
cooperativity_rule.applicability: cooperativity applies ONLY to saturating_cooperative_contact; any other model rejects a non-default value.
cooperativity_rule.nesting: At A0 = 0 both modes reduce to lambda_contact*b(T)*m_total bit for bit.

local_coordination_contact_term.equation: lambda_contact * [b(T)*m_total - A0*sum_i q_i^2/(1 + (q_i/q_sat)^2)], with q_i = k_i/2
local_coordination_contact_term.degree_definition: k_i counts nonbonded wrapped nearest-neighbour beads at monomer i. Covalent neighbours are excluded; intrachain and interchain neighbours enter identically; sum_i k_i = 2*m_total.
local_coordination_contact_term.fit_transfer: h_b, s_b, A0 and q_sat are loaded unchanged from the single-chain fit summary. No multichain refit or parameter rescaling is performed.
local_coordination_contact_term.cooperativity_rule: local is the only valid rule and is the omitted-argument default for this model. An explicit global rule is rejected because it would replace the fitted Hamiltonian with a different m_total/(M*N) model.
local_coordination_contact_term.move_delta_rule: lambda_contact * [b(T)*d_total - A0*delta(sum_i g(k_i))], evaluated from the beads whose local neighbourhood changed.
local_coordination_contact_term.additivity: The state potential is a sum of local monomer terms and is exactly additive over non-interacting chains.
local_coordination_contact_term.nesting: At A0 = 0 the cooperative term is skipped and the potential is exactly lambda_contact*b(T)*m_total.
local_coordination_contact_term.contact_scale: lambda_contact = lambda_intra = lambda_inter; unequal values are rejected because the fitted Hamiltonian is label blind.

contact_quadratic_legacy_rule.equation: lambda_intra * sum_alpha u_contact(m_intra_alpha,T;N) + lambda_inter * b(T) * m_inter
contact_quadratic_legacy_rule.scope: Unchanged since revision 2. The quadratic correction remains per-chain and intrachain only; lambda_intra and lambda_inter stay independent.
contact_quadratic_legacy_rule.prohibited: u_contact MUST NOT be evaluated at the summed intrachain count or at m_intra + m_inter. Because u_contact is nonlinear, two states with equal total intrachain contacts but different per-chain allocations have genuinely different potentials, and collapsing them manufactures artificial cross-chain coupling.

bending_term.independence: The fixed reduced bending penalty is a SEPARATE additive term, never absorbed into any contact model. It is independent of lambda_intra and lambda_inter: setting both lambdas to zero disables the contact interactions but does NOT disable bending when kappa_bend != 0.
bending_term.default: kappa_bend = 0 reproduces the contacts-only sampler exactly.

b_of_T.meaning: reduced contact bias b(T) for the selected contact-bias model, loaded with the SAME semantics as remd_uniform_chain_2_new.py (MODEL_REGISTRY, fitted params, Tref, Tscale).
b_of_T.loading: Loaded through the existing fit_summary.json and model-registry interfaces (resolve_model_params / load_fit_summary_json). Fitted parameters are never modified or refit.
b_of_T.scope_note: b(T) is the FULL potential only for the linear models. For every nonlinear model b(T) is one coefficient of it; potential_definition in the run metadata is the authoritative statement of what was sampled.
b_of_T.single_chain_consistency: For M = 1 and unit contact scale, u reduces to the original single-chain contact potential plus bending.

reduced_potential.nesting: Each nonlinear family nests the linear one at zero extra amplitude: kappa(T) = 0 for contact_quadratic and A0 = 0 for either saturation model reduce u_contact to b(T)*m. At A0 = 0 the value of q_sat has no effect on the potential at all.

effective_energy.label: temperature-dependent EFFECTIVE energy (reported for compatibility only; the reduced potential u is the canonical sampling quantity). It is NOT a temperature-independent microscopic energy.

reduced_potential.label_blindness_criterion: A model may carry independent lambda_intra and lambda_inter if and only if its single-chain u_contact is LINEAR in m. Linearity makes the split exact: b(T)*[l_i*m_intra + l_e*m_inter] is a well-defined Hamiltonian for any (l_i, l_e) and equals l*u_contact(m_total) at l_i = l_e = l, so label-blindness is a special case of the split, not a constraint on it. When u_contact is nonlinear, u_contact(m_intra) + u_contact(m_inter) != u_contact(m_total) and no canonical class-resolved lambda exists, so a single common contact scale is required.

lambda_intra.meaning: coupling multiplier on the intrachain contact term: b(T)*m_intra for the linear models, and the COMPLETE per-chain u_contact (including its nonlinear part) for the contact-quadratic models

lambda_inter.meaning: coupling multiplier on the interchain contact term b(T)*m_inter

lambda_controls.independence: Independent for every model whose u_contact is linear in m (hs) and for the contact-quadratic family. Both saturation models require lambda_intra == lambda_inter because their complete Hamiltonians are label blind; unequal values are rejected. See reduced_potential.label_blindness_criterion.
lambda_controls.note: Equal zero values disable contact energy but leave bending in force.

full_transferability.meaning: null model: a monomer-monomer contact has the same effective free energy whether intra- or interchain (DEFAULT). Available for every model.

independent_collapse.meaning: collapse-only control: interchain contacts carry no free energy. Available for hs and for the contact-quadratic models; rejected by both saturation models.

interchain_attraction_only.meaning: association-only control: intrachain contacts carry no free energy. Available for hs and for the contact-quadratic models; rejected by both saturation models.

athermal_control.meaning: no contact energy; all valid configurations have equal reduced potential. Available for every model.

lambda_controls.pilot_controls: The three-control aggregation pilot is (1,1) equal-contact null, (1,0) collapse-only and (0,1) association-only, run under hs. All three are reachable because hs is linear.

replica_exchange.swap_rule: log_accept = u(X_i, T_i) + u(X_j, T_j) - u(X_j, T_i) - u(X_i, T_j)
replica_exchange.swap_rule_note: The swap evaluates the same state-aware potential as local moves. For saturating_cooperative_contact under cooperativity='global' only m_total enters; local_coordination_saturation uses the complete degree state; for hs and the contact-quadratic models the classified counts enter through lambda_intra and lambda_inter.
replica_exchange.bending_cancels: The fixed reduced bending penalty is temperature-independent and identical within each state, so kappa_bend*(n_i + n_j - n_j - n_i) = 0: it cancels exactly and never enters the swap criterion. There is a single swap rule for all four potential families.
replica_exchange.temperatures: Temperatures are fixed to lanes; complete MultiChainState objects are exchanged between adjacent lanes with even/odd alternation.

local_sweep.definition: 1 local sweep = M * N local move proposals

translation_sweep.definition: 1 translation sweep = M whole-chain translation proposals

sweep_conventions.interface: The run is parameterized by local_sweeps_per_swap and translation_sweeps_per_swap (NOT a single ambiguous absolute steps_per_swap). Both the sweep counts and the actual per-cycle proposal counts are recorded in output metadata.

local.name: end
local.description: move one selected-chain end bead to a random empty neighbor of its anchor bead

local.name: crankshaft
local.description: local corner/kink flip of one interior selected-chain bead about the axis through its two neighbors

local.name: pivot
local.description: rotate a selected-chain tail about a randomly chosen pivot bead using a proper cubic lattice rotation

collective.name: chain_translation
collective.description: translate every bead of one selected chain by one of the six lattice unit vectors; symmetric proposal; own current sites ignored during the interchain collision test; intrachain contacts are exactly preserved and only interchain contacts involving the translated chain are recomputed

invariants: preserve linear connectivity (unit bonds in unwrapped coordinates)
preserve interchain excluded volume via global wrapped occupancy
null proposals (identical to current state) are not counted as state-changing acceptances

contact_updates.debug_path: Recompute full_contact_counts for every geometrically valid trial state (exact oracle).
contact_updates.production_path: Local delta-contact algorithm: enumerate incident canonical contact pairs before the move, build/update a temporary occupancy for the trial, enumerate incident pairs after, canonicalize IDs, determine removed/added intra/inter contacts (deduplicated when multiple moved beads share a contact), and update cached counts.
contact_updates.translation_optimization: Whole-chain translation cannot change intrachain contacts; only interchain contacts involving the translated chain are recomputed.
contact_updates.debug_assertion: An environment-controlled assertion (MULTICHAIN_DEBUG_CONTACTS, analogous to ISAW_DEBUG_CONTACTS) compares cached counts against full_contact_counts after every accepted move.

per_cycle_records: std of per-chain Rg across chains
optional full per-chain Rg vector in diagnostic output
per_chain_geometry.rg_scale_note: rg_scale is applied only to OUTPUT length quantities, never to sampling. Fields suffixed _lattice are raw lattice lengths; the same field without _lattice equals rg_scale times the lattice value (rg_scale**2 for squared lengths). The std of per-chain Rg follows this rule: std_chain_rg_lattice_post is unscaled, std_chain_rg_post = rg_scale * std_chain_rg_lattice_post; init_mean_chain_rg_lattice is unscaled, init_mean_chain_rg = rg_scale * init_mean_chain_rg_lattice.

chain_cluster_graph.edge_rule: connect two chains when they share at least cluster_contact_threshold interchain contacts
records: largest cluster fraction f_max = s_max / M
chain_cluster_graph.note: This is an explicit chain-level graph built from interchain contact pairs; it is NOT the single-chain bead-level contact-graph S_max.

distribution_semantics.P_mean_chain_rg: cycle-level distribution of the MEAN per-chain Rg across chains.
distribution_semantics.P_chain_rg: distribution of POOLED individual-chain Rg samples (all chains, all post-burn-in cycles); resolves homogeneous collapse vs mixed expanded/collapsed chains. Semantically distinct from P_mean_chain_rg.

diagnostics.central_observables_note: Warnings are raised on the raw extensive central observables only; the per-chain normalized series are deterministic transforms and would raise duplicate warnings.

snapshot_format.coordinate_dtype_note: Production snapshots default to int32. The writer allocates the coordinate dtype once from the first snapshot and cannot widen it later, so it never auto-selects int16; int16 remains available only for explicit, size-bounded use. Coordinate canonicalization keeps unwrapped magnitudes bounded so int32 does not overflow.
snapshot_format.note: The single-chain HDF5 schema (T, bead, xyz) is NOT reused for multi-chain coordinates; chain identity is explicit.

initialization.independent_walkers: Each REMD temperature lane begins from its OWN independently generated dispersed state, using deterministic per-lane seeds init_seed = seed + INITIALIZATION_SEED_STRIDE * lane (stride 1000003, distinct from the per-cycle sweep-seed strides). Initialization occurs in the main process so serial and multiprocessing runs share identical starting states.

potential_metadata_contract.purpose: A run's outputs must state the Hamiltonian that was actually sampled, so a reader never has to reconstruct it from the model name.
potential_metadata_contract.potential_kind: one of linear, contact_quadratic, saturating_cooperative, local_coordination_saturation
potential_metadata_contract.potential_definition: the exact single-chain contact potential that was sampled, verbatim from the model registry; local_coordination_saturation is a function of complete state X rather than m alone
potential_metadata_contract.multichain_potential_definition: the exact assembled multi-chain potential: the linear intra/inter split, historical saturation (global or optional local), required local coordination saturation, or the retained contact-quadratic split rule
potential_metadata_contract.potential_normalization: what the state normalization uses: empty for linear models, 'm^2/(2N)' for contact_quadratic, 'q = m/N' for saturating_cooperative, and 'q_i = k_i/2' for local_coordination_saturation
potential_metadata_contract.quadratic_normalization: 'm_chain^2/(2*N)' for contact_quadratic ONLY; empty/null for linear and both saturation families, which have no m^2/(2N) term
potential_metadata_contract.m_ref: contact-number reference used to center q; 0 for every model, recorded explicitly rather than left implicit
potential_metadata_contract.configuration_dependent: true only when the Hamiltonian needs more than contact_count; local_coordination_saturation records true and all legacy models record false
potential_metadata_contract.state_observable: nonbonded_contact_degree_histogram_0_6 for local_coordination_saturation; contact_count for every legacy model
potential_metadata_contract.nonlinear_contact_scope: 'linear_intra_inter_split' for hs; 'all_contacts_global' or 'all_contacts_local_degree' for saturating_cooperative_contact according to its rule; 'all_contacts_local_degree' for local_coordination_saturation; 'intra_per_chain' for contact-quadratic models
potential_metadata_contract.interchain_contact_model: 'same_linear_coefficient_independent_lambda' for hs; 'same_single_chain_potential' for both saturation models; 'linear_coefficient_only' for the retained split models
potential_metadata_contract.runtime_chain_length: the physical beads per chain N; historical global saturation uses M*N explicitly, while local_coordination_saturation uses the fixed q_i=k_i/2 definition and records N as runtime provenance
potential_metadata_contract.fit_chain_length: the N the model was FIT at (provenance only; -1/null when not recorded)
potential_metadata_contract.model_specific_parameters: Models with named domain parameters record them alongside the packed model_params vector: both saturation models write A0 and q_sat.
potential_metadata_contract.additivity_rule: New contract fields are ADDITIVE. Existing field names, types and values are never repurposed, so readers written against an earlier revision keep working.
potential_metadata_contract.quadratic_contact_scope: mirror of nonlinear_contact_scope, retained for readers written against earlier revisions
potential_metadata_contract.cooperativity: 'global' or 'local'; historical saturating_cooperative_contact defaults to global, local_coordination_saturation requires local, and all other models record global

scope_notes: This is the minimum scientifically valid multi-chain simulator to test whether the single-chain contact free energy predicts aggregation.
No PNIPAM-specific extensions beyond the transferability null model are introduced.
Cluster translations, cluster rotations, configurational-bias regrowth, and kinetic acceleration moves are out of scope for this stage.
Reptation is optional and not required for initial completion.
